sources._note: The YC Startup Directory (www.ycombinator.com/companies), an Inertia/React app over an Algolia index. The app id and search-only key are the ones the public page ships to every visitor (captured by watching the page's own XHR, ladder step 4, 2026-09-06); the key is a secured key whose payload pins restrictIndices=YCCompany_production,YCCompany_By_Launch_Date_production and tagFilters=["ycdc_public"], so this reads exactly the rows an anonymous visitor is served. Sliced on `batch` (50 values, largest 398) because the index caps deep pagination at 1000 hits and the book is 6,203.

YC companies absent from the public search index: 76 with live company pages (one of them batch_name 'ycc_only', a Continuity-only holding) and 52 recovered from Internet Archive captures of pages that 404 today. First-party site evidence under §1 either way. See the file's own _readme for how each class was found.

edgar._note: Entity-qualified phrases only, the §1 string-trap rule. 'YC' alone matches 55 EDGAR registrants of which most are namesakes or third-party access vehicles, and bare 'Y Combinator' full-text matches 1,008 filings that are overwhelmingly portfolio companies naming their accelerator, not YC filings — which is exactly what the exit-side sweep wants but is useless as an own-entity pattern. YC's own vehicles all file from 335 Pioneer Way, Mountain View CA; the address is the desk test, never the name (§5 registry rules).

classify._note: The §1 string trap, resolved 2026-09-06. Two distinct external classes share the 'YC' prefix and BOTH would be pulled in by a name rule: (a) third-party access/SPV vehicles that put the YC brand in their own name to sell exposure to a batch — Stonks' per-batch Access Funds, GCW Access - Y Combinator LP, Poolit, the CGF2021/Kolysh/A7/Kepler series SPVs, YC Alums Fund 2021 — every one of them an LP-side feeder, out under T5 (fund-shaped) and T3 (no venture entry by a YC fund); and (b) plain namesakes with no YC connection at all: YCG LLC and YCG Mutual Funds (a Texas asset manager), YCharts, Yclip, YCurb, the Massachusetts YC/YCC/YCH Holdings entities and the New York YCP funds. Resolved by filing address against 335 Pioneer Way, never by the pattern. Two pattern errors were caught by the address test on 2026-09-06 and are recorded because they are the rule proving itself: 'YC Allocate AF26 AI/QP, L.P.' file from 502 Waverley St., Palo Alto — Allocate's address, a private-markets access platform, so they are third-party feeders despite the YC name; and '^ycp[0-9]' had wrongly excluded YCP24 and YCP26, L.P., which file from 335 Pioneer Way and are YC's own Principals vehicles for those batch years. Nothing here is classified by name alone.

eras._note: The directory's per-company namespace, /companies/<slug>. Its job here is NOT recall — the live index carries 6,203 rows including 1,072 Inactive and 815 Acquired, so the directory does not prune its own dead (measured 2026-09-06, and that is the survivorship question §5 tells this layer to answer). Its job is the narrower one of catching companies delisted from the public directory entirely (a company that opted out: the index is tag-filtered to ycdc_public). Captures before ~2018 are the pre-directory site; the earlier YC company list lived only in the batch/Demo Day pages and press, not on a portfolio route (/portfolio* has zero captures in the whole archive). The namespace is larger than CDX's per-query cap, so the era pages the index through CDX's resumption key (cdx_pages/cdx_limit): a single capped query returned only the alphabetical slice '0'-'A' and would have reported survivorship over 4% of the site as if it were the whole layer (found 2026-09-06). RESOLVED 2026-09-07: the era's 2018 and 2019 years returned nothing, and under the zero-rows-is-not-absence rule (Menlo, PRO-91) that had to be established rather than assumed. It is a GENUINE absence. Every 2018-19 capture under /companies/* is the index page itself — 150 captures, zero with a per-company slug segment — and the index was a 3.7KB JS shell with no server-rendered company list, so there is nothing to parse from those years either. YC's per-company URLs begin in 2020, and the era's `from` is set to 2020 accordingly.

roster._note: YC's /people/<slug> namespace. Its job is the profile and the trap set, NOT recall: an accelerator does not take board seats at a rate that makes the Form D related-persons layer work, so the roster-name sweep that is the primary structural layer for a venture firm is near-empty here (issue PRO-74, Phase 2). Partner personal angel positions are the trap class the roster feeds (decisions.md D4). YC's /people page publishes 106 people across 14 sections, of which only 40 are investing roles — President & CEO (1), Partners (17), Founders (4) and Batch group partners (18). The other 66 are Legal, Finance, Media, HR, Policy, Software, Hacker News and operations staff. Same shape as a16z's 469-of-572 non-investor namespace, so site_team_groups constrains the profile's people list to YC's own investing groups (§5 layer 2).

profile._note: focus_min_companies ~4.5% of a 6,200-row base (§11). The directory tags 6,185 of 6,203 rows with its own 59-value industry vocabulary, so the 25% coverage bar is cleared with room to spare — the first investor since a16z failed it where the recompute can actually publish. The crosswalk into the closed twelve is filled at the profile step, never adopted verbatim.
profile._focus_note: Two-layer crosswalk, and the two layers answer different questions. The directory's INDUSTRY vocabulary (subindustry, 59 values, 100% coverage) has no AI value at all and no crypto value — YC files AI companies under B2B/Consumer like anything else — so an industry-only crosswalk would publish a focus distribution with an empty AI & Applied AI bucket on the investor that has funded more AI companies than any other. The TAG vocabulary (336 values, 5,324/6,203 rows = 85.8%) carries exactly what is missing: Artificial Intelligence 998, AI 894, Generative AI 255, Machine Learning 238, plus Blockchain, Cybersecurity and Developer Tools. So tags are consulted first and subindustry is the 100%-coverage fallback. §6's precedence rules still govern where the two disagree, and 'AI is the product, not that the company uses ML' stays a judgment the grind makes per row — the crosswalk proposes, it does not publish. A further finding at profile time: the profile's focus RECOMPUTE reads the base's `sector` column, which carries the directory's INDUSTRY vocabulary only — so a recompute off it would publish a SaaS-heavy distribution with an empty AI bucket, the exact failure the two-layer crosswalk exists to prevent. The published investment_scope.focus is therefore the curated list, which is ordered by the judged `focus` column (AI & Applied AI 1,407, SaaS 1,220, Fintech & Payments 782, Consumer & Marketplaces 776, DevTools & APIs 576, Healthcare & Bio 513, Industrial & Robotics 417). That is a deliberate choice, not the recompute silently failing.

shape._note: Set to YC's own properties, not the megafund defaults (§8 lesson 5: base-shape guards are investor properties). A seed accelerator's book is mostly small: of 6,203 directory rows 1,072 read Inactive and 4,293 Active, and YC's own top_company flag marks 91 rows — so the $1B+ share belongs near 2-4%, and a 20% guard would never fire on anything. The C2A guard is the one that matters here: this is the firm the column was designed for, thousands of seed entries, and an accelerator's seed-to-A graduation rate is well under a lead investor's (Accel published 79.1% on 91 rows of led seeds; YC's cohort is every batch company). Both restated in decisions.md against the evidence; the guards still fire above these.

verify._known_positions_note: 'mercury' and 'goodleap' removed 2026-09-07. Mercury is in this run's own membership TRAP set with a not_member answer — Immad Akhund founded Heyzap (YC W09) and was a YC part-time partner, but Mercury itself never did a batch and no YC fund is on its cap table. Listing it as a known position would have made the trap set and the verify guard contradict each other. GoodLeap is likewise not a YC company. 'boom supersonic' is left in and is a genuine open recall question.
verify._unicorn_note: Rule A (Erik, 2026-09-06): the unicorn snapshot is an aggregator — a coverage floor to verify, never a mark. With this false the list still flags a row for the web pass but never writes a figure or a band, so a name-matched aggregator entry cannot override a judged below_1b. YC needs it because the list name-matched unrelated companies onto its rows (cohere at $6.8B onto a S20 company the directory marks Acquired).
verify._c2a_note: S2A does not apply to this book at all (Erik, 2026-09-19): YC is a pre-seed investor, every row enters on the batch deal's standard terms and carries entry_stage Pre-Seed sourced program_terms, so the column is null throughout rather than `undetermined` throughout. The transition this cohort actually makes is pre-seed to seed, which the dataset does not measure. c2a_deterministic stays false so nothing re-queues the column; the older reason for declining it still holds too (YC companies raise on SAFEs under 4(a)(2) and file no Form D, so establishing a seed-to-A transition would take ~5,000 web checks, report.md 4).
